traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and listed requirements for Story 002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG are fully implemented and verified:
- Core Functionality & REQ-CONFIG-PRESETS/REQ-FLAT-CONFIG: `src/index.ts` defines `configs.recommended` and `configs.strict` as ESLint v9 flat-config arrays (objects with only `rules`). `tests/config/flat-config-presets-integration.test.ts` uses `FlatESLint` with `[baseConfig, ...configs.recommended]` and `[baseConfig, ...configs.strict]` and confirms that the `traceability/require-story-annotation` rule is enabled, directly satisfying REQ-CONFIG-PRESETS and demonstrating correct flat-config behavior. - Quality Standards & Integration: The presets are intentionally minimal (only rule severity mappings) so they compose cleanly with other flat-config entries (e.g., `js.configs.recommended`). Integration tests show they work when spread after a `plugins` registration object, evidencing seamless integration without conflicting with other config aspects. - REQ-CUSTOMIZABLE-PATHS: `src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts` exposes `storyDirectories`, `allowAbsolutePaths`, and `requireStoryExtension` options with defaults and uses them in its logic. Tests in `tests/rules/valid-story-reference.test.ts` (see Jest output for `[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS]` cases) confirm these options work and respect project boundaries. - REQ-RULE-OPTIONS & REQ-CONFIG-VALIDATION: Both `valid-story-reference` and `require-story-annotation` define explicit JSON-schema-like `meta.schema` with `additionalProperties: false`. Config tests (`tests/config/eslint-config-validation.test.ts` and `tests/config/require-story-annotation-config.test.ts`) verify the expected properties exist and that ESLint throws helpful, specific errors on unknown options and type mismatches, satisfying the Error Handling acceptance criterion. - REQ-PROJECT-INTEGRATION & User Experience: `user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md` and `README.md` provide clear examples for JavaScript-only, TypeScript, mixed JS/TS projects, monorepos, test files, and a full working example for a plugin project. These docs show exactly how to register the plugin and spread `traceability.configs.recommended`/`strict`, fulfilling the documentation, integration, and usability criteria. - All relevant tests for this story (config presets integration, config validation, rule option schemas, and related rule behavior) pass under `npm test` with Jest.
Given the concrete implementation and passing tests directly tied to the story’s requirements and acceptance criteria, this story is judged fully implemented.
